children: By Hikaru Sunaga and Kaname Sugimoto / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writers
Japan Post Bank Co. is considering acquiring a stake of about 20% in Matsui Securities Co., a major Japanese online brokerage firm, according to sources.

By partnering with a major securities firm, Japan Post Bank aims to expand its services to include letting users of its savings accounts buy and sell stocks and other securities. The new service is expected to launch as early as 2027. By expanding its range of financial services, the bank hopes to expand its connection with customers in the asset management area.
Both companies are expected to decide on whether to proceed with the deal at board meetings possibly in early November.
Japan Post Bank is expected to acquire enough shares to make it, by itself, the largest shareholder in Matsui Securities, after which it plans to dispatch one of its own directors to the company.

Japan Post Bank has about 120 million savings accounts, making it one of the largest banks in Japan. Its retail asset management services are currently focused primarily on the sale of mutual funds and government bonds. Through the envisaged investment, the bank plans to integrate its Yucho Bankbook App, which allows users to check balances and transfer funds via smartphone, with Matsui Securities' systems, thereby enabling Japan Post Bank customers to conduct stock, FX and other types of trading. Matsui Securities will handle the opening of securities accounts and trading itself, while Japan Post Bank will serve as a bridge between customers and securities investments.

As of the end of March 2026, Japan Post Bank's ordinary savings balance stood at about 186 trillion yen, and it had a network of over 23,000 outlets, primarily at post offices. In its medium-term management plan for fiscal 2026-2028, the bank set a goal of becoming a "comprehensive financial platform" capable of meeting customers' diverse financial needs. As part of this, it said it would consider partnerships with securities firms as a potential strategy to address demand for a service that would allow users to manage assets such as stocks and bonds. The bank also aims to expand the number of registered accounts on its app from the current level of somewhat more than 16 million to 25 million by fiscal 2028.

Matsui Securities, founded in 1918, is known as a pioneer in online brokerage, having launched Japan's first full-scale online trading service in 1998. The company has gained popularity among individual investors thanks to its strengths in services such as margin trading, which allows customers to trade amounts several times their initial capital using stocks or cash as collateral.

However, as of the end of September, Matsui Securities' total number of accounts stood at about 1.83 million, just over one-tenth of the number held by SBI Securities Co.--about 16.38 million as of the end of June--or Rakuten Securities Inc.--about 14.39 million as of the same date. It is believed that Matsui Securities aims to acquire new customers through Japan Post Bank's customer base and branch network.

Matsui Securities President and CEO Akira Warita did not make explicit comments regarding the possible partnership during a financial results press conference Wednesday. "If we were to partner with any entity, it would be on the condition that it would lead to the expansion of our customer base and our range of products and services," he said.
